subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: The Lord’s Prayer
overview: Jesus taught his followers how to pray in Matthew 6:9-13. This prayer is called the Lord's Prayer. In this sub-strand you will recite it, learn what each part means, pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives, and make prayer a daily habit so that you grow spiritually.

lessons.title: Reciting the Lord's Prayer
objectives: Recite the Lord's Prayer from memory.
lessons.intro: Jesus did not leave his followers without words for prayer. In Matthew 6:9-13 he said, "This is how you should pray," and gave them the prayer Christians still recite.
lessons.notes:
### Where the prayer is found
Read Matthew 6:9-13. Jesus was teaching his disciples. He told them to pray in this way. Christians call it the Lord's Prayer because the Lord Jesus taught it.

Learn to recite it. The words below follow Matthew 6:9-13. Many churches end with the words of praise that the King James Bible includes in verse 13.

Our Father in heaven,
hallowed be your name.
Your kingdom come.
Your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us today our daily bread.
And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

### How to learn it
- Read one sentence.
- Say it with the teacher.
- Cover the page and say it again.
- Add the next sentence only when the first one is firm.
- Recite it with a partner, then alone.

Say the words clearly. Do not rush the middle lines about forgiveness and temptation, because those lines are easy to skip. "Amen" means "so be it". It is the way we end the prayer, agreeing with what we have asked.

### Recite it daily
The design asks learners to recite the Lord's Prayer daily. Morning, before lessons, or evening is a good time. Reciting is not a race. It is speaking to God the prayer Jesus gave. In the next lesson you will look at what each line is asking. For this lesson, the aim is to know the words and to say them correctly.

A song that uses the Lord's Prayer can help the memory. Sing it, then speak it without the tune, so that you can recite it even when there is no music.

keyWords.meaning: the prayer Jesus taught his followers in Matthew 6:9-13
so be it; the word that ends the prayer

activity.title: Read and recite Matthew 6:9-13
materials: Flash cards with each line of the prayer
steps: Sing a song related to the Lord's Prayer.
Arrange flash cards of the lines in the correct order.
Recite the Lord's Prayer in pairs, then as a class, until you can say it without the cards.

practice.question: In which passage did Jesus teach the Lord's Prayer?
Recite the Lord's Prayer.
practice.answer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

practice.question: What does "Amen" mean at the end of the prayer?
practice.answer: So be it. We agree with the prayer we have prayed.

practice.question: Why is this prayer called the Lord's Prayer?
practice.answer: Because the Lord Jesus taught it to his followers.

summary: Jesus taught the Lord's Prayer in Matthew 6:9-13.
It begins "Our Father in heaven" and ends with praise and Amen.
Christians recite it daily, carefully and from memory.

lessons.title: What the prayer asks
objectives: Explain the meaning of each part of the Lord's Prayer.
Give reasons for praying to God every day.
lessons.intro: Saying the words is the first step. Understanding them keeps the prayer from becoming empty sound. Each line of Matthew 6:9-13 asks God for something, or honours him.
lessons.notes:
### The meaning of the lines
- "Our Father in heaven": We pray to God as Father. "Our" means we pray with other people, not only for ourselves. He is in heaven, above us and holy.
- "Hallowed be your name": We ask that God's name be honoured as holy in our words and in our lives.
- "Your kingdom come": We ask God to reign. We want his rule in our hearts and in the world.
- "Your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven": We ask to do what God wants, here, in the same way heaven does his will.
- "Give us today our daily bread": We ask for what we need this day, beginning with food. We depend on God for daily needs.
- "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors": Debts here mean our sins. We ask God to forgive us, and we forgive people who have wronged us. The two belong together in the prayer Jesus taught.
- "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil": We ask God to keep us from falling into sin and to rescue us from the evil one.
- "For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever": We end by praising God. The kingdom, power and glory are his. Amen.

### Why pray every day
Prayer is talking with God. Jesus taught his followers to pray, so prayer is part of Christian life, not an extra for Sundays only.

- We thank God.
- We ask for daily needs.
- We ask for forgiveness and for strength against temptation.
- We grow spiritually. A person who speaks with God every day stays close to him and learns to want what God wants.

You can pray in the morning, at meals, in the evening, and whenever you are afraid or thankful. Reciting the Lord's Prayer can be one of those times. Other simple prayers, in your own words, belong in the day as well.

Discuss this with the class: a day with no prayer is a day in which we forget to speak to our Father. A short prayer is better than none.

keyWords.meaning: what God wants to be done
in this prayer, the sins for which we need forgiveness
a pull towards sin; we ask God not to let us fall into it
to become closer to God and stronger in faith

activity.title: Match each line to its meaning
steps: In groups, discuss why it is important to pray every day.
Write each line of the Lord's Prayer on a strip and, beside it, the meaning in your own words.
Recite the prayer daily. List how many times you prayed yesterday and be ready to share the number with classmates in the next lesson.

practice.question: What are we asking when we say "Hallowed be your name"?
practice.answer: That God's name will be honoured as holy.

practice.question: What does "Give us today our daily bread" ask for?
practice.answer: Our needs for the day, beginning with food.

practice.question: What do "debts" mean in the Lord's Prayer, and what must we also do?
practice.answer: Our sins. We ask God to forgive us, and we forgive our debtors, the people who have wronged us.

practice.question: Give two reasons why a Christian should pray every day.
practice.answer: Any two: Jesus taught us to pray; we thank God and ask for our needs; we ask for forgiveness and help against temptation; we grow spiritually by staying close to God.

summary: Each line of the Lord's Prayer honours God or asks for his help.
We ask for daily needs, forgiveness, and deliverance from evil.
Praying every day helps a Christian grow spiritually.

lessons.title: Praying for others every day
objectives: Pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives.
Plan a daily time of prayer.
lessons.intro: The Lord's Prayer says "our" and "us", not only "my" and "me". Jesus taught us to pray with other people in mind. Christians pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives, and they do it every day.
lessons.notes:
### Who we pray for
Unity grows when we bring other people to God instead of thinking only of ourselves.

- Parents and guardians: thank God for them. Ask him to give them health, work, wisdom and peace. Ask him to help you honour them.
- Friends: ask God to help them at school, to keep them safe, and to help you be a kind and truthful friend.
- Relatives: brothers, sisters, grandparents and other family members. Pray for those who are sick, those who are away, and those who do not yet know God.

You do not need long words. "Lord, bless my mother and keep her safe today" is a real prayer. You may also use the Lord's Prayer and then add these names.

### A daily prayer
Choose a time you can keep: after waking, before you sleep, or both. In that time:

1. Recite the Lord's Prayer.
2. Thank God for one thing.
3. Pray for a parent or guardian, a friend and a relative by name.
4. Ask God to keep you from sin today.
5. End with Amen.

Count the times you pray in a day and share the number with classmates. The number is not a competition. It helps you see whether prayer is really happening. If you prayed only once, you can add an evening prayer. If you forgot, begin again the next morning. Self-discipline grows when the recital is daily, not only when the teacher is listening.

### Growing spiritually
Spiritual growth is a closer walk with God. Daily prayer is one way it happens. You remember that God is Father, that you need forgiveness, and that other people need his help too. A class that prays for one another is a class that is learning the "our" of the Lord's Prayer.

keyWords.meaning: a person who cares for a child in the place of a parent
speaking to God every day, not only sometimes

activity.title: Pray for people we love
steps: Pray for your parents or guardians, your friends and your relatives. You may pray aloud or quietly.
List the number of times you prayed yesterday or today and share the number with a classmate.
Write a simple daily plan: the time you will pray, and three people you will name.

practice.question: Name three groups of people Christians should pray for in this lesson.
practice.answer: Parents or guardians, friends, and relatives.

practice.question: Give one thing you can ask God for on behalf of your parents or guardians.
practice.answer: Any one real need, for example health, work, wisdom, peace, or help as they care for the family.

practice.question: What can you include in a daily prayer time?
practice.answer: The Lord's Prayer, thanks, prayer for a parent or guardian, a friend and a relative, a prayer for help against sin, and Amen.

practice.question: Why does daily prayer help you grow spiritually?
practice.answer: It keeps you close to God, reminds you to depend on him, and teaches you to care for other people before him.

summary: Pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives by name.
Recite the Lord's Prayer every day and add your own thanks and requests.
Daily prayer helps Christians grow spiritually and live in unity.

quiz.question: Where is the Lord's Prayer written?
quiz.explanation: Jesus taught this prayer in Matthew 6:9-13.

quiz.question: The Lord's Prayer begins with:
quiz.explanation: Matthew 6:9 starts the prayer with Our Father in heaven.

quiz.question: "Hallowed be your name" means:
options: May your name be honoured as holy

quiz.question: In the Lord's Prayer, "debts" means:
options: The tables of the money changers
quiz.explanation: We ask God to forgive our sins, as we forgive those who wrong us.

quiz.question: Recite the two lines that ask God to forgive us and to keep us from evil.
quiz.answer: Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
quiz.explanation: These lines are part of Matthew 6:12-13.

quiz.question: Why should a Christian pray every day?
options: So that other people will praise them
To talk with God, receive help, and grow spiritually
quiz.explanation: Daily prayer keeps a believer close to God.

quiz.question: Which people should you pray for?
options: Parents or guardians, friends and relatives
Only strangers you will never meet
Nobody; the Lord's Prayer forbids names
quiz.explanation: The lesson guides learners to pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives.

quiz.question: Give one prayer you can say for a friend.
quiz.answer: Any suitable request, for example: Lord, help my friend to learn well and to be safe.
quiz.explanation: Praying for friends is part of caring for them before God.

quiz.question: What does a daily prayer time help you to do?
quiz.explanation: Saying a prayer to God every day helps a Christian grow spiritually.

quiz.question: Why does the prayer say "our" Father and "our" daily bread?
quiz.answer: We pray together and we include other people, not only ourselves.
quiz.explanation: The plural words teach unity and care for others.
